newsitem.title: USA: CME plans GLOBEX stock index futures rules changes.
newsitem.headline: CME plans GLOBEX stock index futures rules changes.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange board has proposed changing its rules on opening times and price limits for stock index futures traded on GLOBEX, according to a notice issued to CME members Monday.
The changes, which the CME board proposed at a November 18 meeting, need Commodity Futures Trading Commission approval.

On days when a New York Stock Exchange-coordinated trading halt was in effect or futures were locked limit up or down at the close of regular hours, the CME wants to delay the GLOBEX opening in U.S. stock index futures until 1800 CST/0000 GMT.
Stock futures on the GLOBEX after-hours electronic trading system normally open at 1545 CST/2145 GMT.
The CME said the amendment would help coordinate trading halts for different stock index contracts. It would codify policy that has been in effect since November 1993.

The CME board also proposed changing the way it calculates price limits on Standard & Poor's 500 futures for the GLOBEX session. Under the proposal, the settlement price at the end of daytime trading would be the reference price for calculating price limits through the entire GLOBEX session.

Currently, the reference price for GLOBEX price-limit purposes is the 1245 CST/1845 GMT price up to 1800 CST, when the settlement price becomes the reference price. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
